title: Task sync stage 1: structured refusal and candidate retention for TermAl-responsible runs
outcome: Task sync stage 1: structured refusal and candidate retention for TermAl-responsible runs
acceptance: Before any final planning or receipt mutation, the complete affected run/claim/local basis is discovered and revalidated; any affected run with TermAl responsibility, or with unproven responsibility/settlement, refuses the whole final batch with a stable distinct code (reserved: task_sync_host_responsibility), plus distinct causes for a moved candidate/readset basis, an immutable-operation intent conflict and a pending hold

On refusal the candidate bytes and identity are retained, and no graph, receipt or cursor advances, no claim is released or run retired, no prompt is cleared and nothing is dispatched; exact retries keep candidate and operation identity; the same key with changed input refuses

No Engram-only query, quiet period, elapsed time, dead host, crash or restart is accepted as settlement; host-unreachable, mid-turn cut, unsettled carried check, uncertain Begin/Evaluate and late-dispatch cases are retained, proven by tests
